title: Unity and Godot users.. How do you use AI to texture your walls and floors? Having a hard time. Don't want advertisement comments
author: SquirrelTomahawk
selftext: Anybody found useful method on getting texturized walls and floors they made with AI? Thanks

comments.author: fued
comments.body: I just use an asset pack

replies.author: Aesthetic-Engine
replies.body: This is a really good answer to a lot of the questions in the sub. So many cheap and free packs out there. Plus your LLM can probably customize them to make them feel like your own.

replies.author: Aesthetic-Engine
replies.body: I'm building off this [Low Poly Sci-Fi/Cyberpunk pack](https://justcreate3d.itch.io/low-poly-sci-fi-cyberpunk-city) and I recently picked up [Ultimate Clouds and Sky for Godot](https://worsteventgames.itch.io/ultimate-clouds-and-sky-for-godot-4x). Both were well worth the small cost!

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Damn I like the look of the sci fi one but I need building that have interiors as well

replies.author: miomao10
replies.body:
This is really nice. So can I ask, do I just give the ai all the resources and it builds with these assets? Like does this work for any assets and documentation on the unity store? Plug into the ai and it can try to make the vision with the assets? So I could be using models for cheap with animations.

Also- lots of features on unity asset store cost money, I have been thinking of just making the feature with the ai to skip using their tools. Seems practical for some use cases.

replies.author: fued
replies.body:
AI costs money too, often far more.

And no, you need to work out a workflow that works for you

replies.author: miomao10
replies.body: So far creating my own tools and extensions for my browser and replacing programs has been well worth the cost

replies.author: Aesthetic-Engine
replies.body:
I build in Godot using Cursor and my tool Godot Runtime Bridge. So I asked Cursor to first inventory the asset pack and create a reference guide .md file to the pack that coding agents reference to build. 

The game I'm making uses procedural generation based on a song you input so I uploaded my asset reference guide to Gemini and did a deep research prompt to get design advice for utilizing the asset pack to generate tracks. Cursor and the other models I use just use the deep research report and the reference guide and over time I built a procedural generation engine. 

But yes if your tool connects to and works with your editor you should be able to instruct it how to build what you want from the assets you bought.

replies.author: miomao10
replies.body: Reference it up and then workflow got it

comments.author: Hot-Spare5735
comments.body:
You can ask AI image generators to make "tileable" textures. As for whatever you want it to look like. 


I would recommend just watching general tutorials for how to create textures walls with non-AI methods and then figure out how to use AI to do it for you.


That is my recommendation for every part of game art.

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: It takes like 30 seconds of clone brush to take a non seamless texture and turn it into a seamless texture. Look up a vid of ai isn't getting it right

comments.author: Olmeca_Gold
comments.body: Use patina from fal if you actually want tileable textures

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body: The method I used was really inconvenient. I would use that tool from Gimp that would shift the pixels of the image by width/2 and height/2, wrapping them around, and use this image for requesting the AI to paint over it - so I would mask the parts where the textures would cause the seam and request the AI to replace them. It worked, but it was a tedious process, probably better solutions out there.
